Title: Modified Mercalli Scale of Earthquake Intensity
Rows: `text(I)`
Not felt except by a very few under especially favorable conditions.
`text(II)`
Felt only by a few persons at rest, especially on upper floors of buildings.
`text(III)`

Felt quite noticeably by persons indoors, especially on upper floors of buildings. Many people do not recognize it as an earthquake. Parked cars may rock slightly. Vibrations similar to the passing of a truck.
`text(IV)`

Felt indoors by many, outdoors by few during the `text(day)`. At night, some awakened. Dishes, windows, doors disturbed; walls make cracking sound. Sensation like heavy truck striking building. Parked cars rocked noticeably.
`text(V)`
Felt by nearly everyone; many awakened. Some dishes, windows broken. Unstable objects overturned. Pendulum clocks may stop.
`text(VI)`
Felt by all, many frightened. Some heavy furniture moved; a few instances of fallen plaster. Damage slight.
`text(VII)`

Damage minimal in buildings of good design and construction; slight to moderate in well-built ordinary structures; considerable damage in poorly built or badly designed structures; some chimneys broken.
`text(VIII)`

Damage slight in specially designed structures; considerable damage with partial collapse in ordinary substantial buildings. Damage great in poorly built structures. Fall of chimneys, factory stacks, columns, monuments, walls. Heavy furniture overturned.
`text(IX)`
Damage considerable in specially designed structures; well-designed frame structures tilted. Damage great in substantial buildings, with partial collapse. Buildings shifted off foundations.
`text(X)`
Most masonry and frame structures and foundations are destroyed. Train rails bent.
`text(XI)`
Few, if any, structures remain standing. Bridges destroyed. Train rails bent greatly.
`text(XII)`
Damage total. Objects thrown into the air.
